newsitem.title: USA: Latam deals dominate U.S. foreign crude scene.
newsitem.headline: Latam deals dominate U.S. foreign crude scene.

text.p: Latin American transactions dominated the U.S. foreign crude scene on Thursday, as many Gulf Coast traders headed out early for the U.S. Independence Day holiday on Friday.
In Colombia, the first three August loaders of closely watched Cusiana crude were sold, setting the tone for the month's sales, traders said.
Colombian state oil company Ecopetrol sold two early August cargoes of Cusiana crude oil to a U.S. refiner at 95 cents a barrel under West Texas Intermediate/Cushing, trade sources said.
The 550,000 barrel cargoes, which load August 4-8 and August 10-14, are likely to be co-loaded into the U.S. Gulf Coast.
Traders said the buyer was planning to keep one cargo and resell the other.
Equity producer British Petroleum also sold a separate Cusiana cargo loading August 1-5 after Ecopetrol's transactions at an undisclosed discount to September WTI, traders said.
Elsewhere in the region, Chile's state oil company Empresa Nacional del Petroleo (ENAP) bought Angolan Palanca and Ecuadoran Oriente crude cargoes for August 14-18 delivery, traders said.
ENAP bought the 950,000 barrel Palanca from a European company at an undisclosed price related to Dated Brent.

The firm purchased the 380,000 barrel Oriente from an Ecuadoran trading house at a small premium to the price formula for Chilean customers, which is $5.18 under West Texas Intermediate/Cushing, trade sources said.
Separately, traders were awaiting the results of a purchase tender for one million barrels of crude called by Uruguay's state oil refiner ANCAP for August 18-28 delivery.
The Uruguayan tender will be awarded late on Thursday.

Trans-Atlantic activity was subdued on Thursday. Traders reiterated, however, that the slightly widening WTI/Brent spread, coupled with feeble refining margins in Europe, should encourage North Sea crude offerings into the U.S. Gulf.
Brent was assessed around WTI minus 35 cents a barrel delivered into the Gulf in August.
The August spread was around $1.30-40 a barrel early on Thursday afternoon, steady with Wednesday but up around five to 10 cents from Tuesday.
